title: A pool of threads and their futures

terminal.description: A shell in your workspace. Run the morning's bookings here; each confirmation takes the office about a second.

tasks.title: Confirm the bookings with a pool of three
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 1`, write a class `Batch` with one method, with `throws InterruptedException, ExecutionException`. `static List<String> confirmAll(List<String> bookings, Office office)` makes a pool of exactly three threads, hands it one job per booking that gives back `office.confirm(booking)`, and gives back the confirmations in the order of the bookings. A booking that fails reaches the caller as the `ExecutionException` that `get` throws. Whatever happens, the pool is shut down before `confirmAll` returns. `Office` is given above the tasks.

Check hands `confirmAll` bookings and an office of its own. The office holds every job until `confirmAll` is waiting for an answer, and Check counts the pool's threads at that moment and every thread that ran a job. It reads the confirmations, sees whether a failed booking reaches it, and whether any thread of the pool is still alive afterwards.
nextSteps: Read the parts of the lesson about a pool, submit and get.
Make the pool, and a list for the futures.
In one loop hand over every job; in a second, get every answer.
Shut the pool down in a finally, so that it happens whatever get throws.
hints: The lesson builds a pool, hands it jobs and reads their answers in three short steps: this task is those steps for a list.

A job that gives back an answer is a Callable: a lambda with no parameters that returns something, and may throw. Its Future holds the answer later. A get straight after each hand-over waits for that job before the next one is handed over.

`ExecutorService pool = Executors.newFixedThreadPool(3);` then `try { ... futures.add(pool.submit(() -> office.confirm(booking))); ... confirmations.add(future.get()); ... } finally { pool.shutdown(); }`.

tasks.title: Keep going past a booking that fails
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 2`, write a class `Careful` with one method, with `throws InterruptedException`. `static List<String> confirmEach(ExecutorService pool, List<String> bookings, Office office, List<String> problems)` hands the pool it is given one job per booking, as Task 1 does, and gives back the confirmations of the bookings that worked, in their order. A booking whose job threw is left out, and its problem is added to `problems`, in the order of the bookings: the booking, a colon and a space, then the message of what its job threw, as in `Fisher, 1: the office line dropped`. The pool belongs to the caller: `confirmEach` leaves it open.

Check hands `confirmEach` a pool of its own, which counts the jobs it is handed and notes a shutdown, and an office of its own that fails some bookings with an `IOException` and holds every job until `confirmEach` is waiting for an answer. It reads the confirmations, the problems, how many jobs had been handed to its pool when the first answer was awaited, and whether the pool was left open.
nextSteps: Read the part of the lesson about what get throws.
Hand over the jobs as in Task 1, to the pool you are given.
Get each answer inside a try of its own, and catch what get throws when a job failed.
Read the problem's message from what the job itself threw.
hints: The lesson shows the stack trace of a failed job: two exceptions, one inside the other.

get wraps what the job threw in an ExecutionException, whose own message starts with the inner exception's class name. The inner one is its cause. A try around the whole loop ends the loop at the first failure.
For each future: `try { confirmations.add(futures.get(i).get()); } catch (ExecutionException e) { problems.add(bookings.get(i) + ": " + e.getCause().getMessage()); }`.

tasks.title: Keep one pool open for the day
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 3`, write a class `Desk` that keeps one pool for the whole day. `Desk(int threads)` makes a pool of that many threads. `List<String> confirmAll(List<String> bookings, Office office)`, with `throws InterruptedException, ExecutionException`, hands that pool a job per booking all at once with `invokeAll` and gives back the confirmations in the order of the bookings; a booking that fails reaches the caller as the `ExecutionException` that `get` throws, and the pool stays open. `void close()` shuts the pool down.

Check makes a desk of two threads, has it confirm two lists, and closes it. It counts every thread that ran a job of either list, sees whether the answers were awaited inside `invokeAll`, whether a failed booking reaches it and the desk still works afterwards, whether a closed desk refuses new bookings with a `RejectedExecutionException`, and whether any thread is still alive after `close`.
nextSteps: Read the parts of the lesson about invokeAll and about shutting a pool down.
Make the pool in the constructor and keep it in a field.
In confirmAll, build a list of jobs first, then hand them all over at once.
Shut the pool down in close, and only there.
hints: A pool is worth keeping: its threads are made once and do job after job. A pool made in each call makes new threads every time.
invokeAll takes a whole list of Callables, waits until all are done, and gives back their futures in the same order. A pool that is shut down takes no more jobs.

`pool = Executors.newFixedThreadPool(threads);` in the constructor; in confirmAll, `jobs.add(() -> office.confirm(booking));` for each booking, then `for (Future<String> f : pool.invokeAll(jobs)) confirmations.add(f.get());`; in close, `pool.shutdown();`.
